newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees inflation to fall to 2.5 pct by 2006.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees inflation to fall to 2.5 pct by 2006.

text.p: Hungary expects to reduce annual inflation to 2.5 percent by 2006 from a forecast of 18 percent for this year, the government said on Monday.

In an appendix to the draft pension reform, recently submitted to parliament, the government said the inflation level of 2.5 percent would fulfil the membership criteria of the European Monetary Union (EMU).
Hungary hopes to become member of the European Union (EU), and also the EMU, in the first years of the next century.
The document, published by the Finance Ministry, added that Hungary expected the gross domestic product (GDP) to grow by 4.5 to five percent annually in the years following 2000.
Hungary earlier forecast three percent GDP growth for 1997 and four to five percent for the following few years.
The new pension system adds a fully funded component to the old pay-as-you-go system.
Finance Ministry deputy state secretary Laszlo Akar told a news conference that the parliament is likely to approve the pension reform in July, and the law takes effect in 1998.
The reform will introduce private pension funds, which are expected to manage assets equivalent to 10 percent of GDP by the years after 2010, and 30 percent by 2025, the ministry said.
